packs.title: Discourse markers, fixed expressions and collocations

words.note: opens the first point of an argument; formal, mainly written register

example.target: En primer lugar, quiero agradecer a todos vuestro esfuerzo.
example.gloss: First of all, I want to thank you all for your effort.

words.note: introduces the second point after en primer lugar; formal register

example.target: En segundo lugar, hay que revisar el presupuesto.
example.gloss: Secondly, the budget needs to be reviewed.

words.note: formal connector that states a logical result, mainly written

example.target: No llegamos a un acuerdo y, por consiguiente, la reunión se aplazó.
example.gloss: We did not reach an agreement and, therefore, the meeting was postponed.

words.note: formal, states the result of what was just said

example.target: El vuelo se canceló; en consecuencia, tuvimos que cambiar los planes.
example.gloss: The flight was cancelled; as a result, we had to change our plans.

words.note: closes a concession; works in speech and writing; note that aun here carries no accent, unlike aún (still)

example.target: Llovía muchísimo, aun así salimos a caminar.
example.gloss: It was raining a lot, even so we went out for a walk.

words.note: introduces a concession before a noun or infinitive; neutral to formal

example.target: A pesar del tráfico, llegamos a tiempo.
example.gloss: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.

words.note: contrasts two facts; neutral register

example.target: Ana prefiere el campo, mientras que su hermano prefiere la ciudad.
example.gloss: Ana prefers the countryside, whereas her brother prefers the city.

words.note: introduces an opposing idea; more formal than en cambio

example.target: No se enfadó; por el contrario, se echó a reír.
example.gloss: He did not get angry; on the contrary, he burst out laughing.

words.note: rephrases what was just said; formal, mainly written

example.target: El proyecto no es viable, dicho de otro modo, no tenemos suficiente dinero.
example.gloss: The project is not viable, put another way, we do not have enough money.

words.note: rephrases an idea more simply; neutral, spoken and written

example.target: No podemos permitírnoslo, en otras palabras, es demasiado caro.
example.gloss: We cannot afford it, in other words, it is too expensive.

words.note: narrows a general statement to something specific

example.target: Me gusta la música, en concreto, el jazz.
example.gloss: I like music, specifically, jazz.

words.note: signals the most important point; neutral to formal

example.target: Ante todo, quiero deciros que estoy muy orgulloso de vosotros.
example.gloss: First and foremost, I want to tell you that I am very proud of you.

words.note: sums up an argument before closing it; neutral register

example.target: Hemos discutido mucho, pero en definitiva, la decisión es tuya.
example.gloss: We have discussed a lot, but in the end, the decision is yours.

words.note: opens the closing part of a written argument; formal

example.target: En conclusión, el plan necesita más tiempo.
example.gloss: In conclusion, the plan needs more time.

words.note: signals the last point of a spoken or written argument; neutral

example.target: Para terminar, me gustaría dar las gracias al equipo.
example.gloss: To finish, I would like to thank the team.

words.note: formal, mainly written; usually followed by que

example.target: Cabe destacar que el proyecto se terminó antes de lo previsto.
example.gloss: It should be noted that the project finished ahead of schedule.

words.note: impersonal formula that introduces a factor the listener must consider; more formal than the plain phrase tener en cuenta

example.target: Hay que tener en cuenta que el examen es el lunes.
example.gloss: It must be taken into account that the exam is on Monday.

words.note: reports something without full certainty; neutral, spoken and written

example.target: Según parece, van a subir los precios del billete.
example.gloss: Apparently, they are going to raise the ticket prices.

words.note: reports secondhand information; neutral register

example.target: Al parecer, el jefe se va de la empresa.
example.gloss: Apparently, the boss is leaving the company.

words.note: explicitly frames what follows as a personal opinion; neutral to formal

example.target: Desde mi punto de vista, deberíamos esperar un poco más.
example.gloss: From my point of view, we should wait a little longer.

words.note: introduces a personal opinion; neutral, common in speech and writing

example.target: En mi opinión, la película es demasiado larga.
example.gloss: In my opinion, the film is too long.

words.note: more formal way of introducing an opinion than en mi opinión

example.target: A mi juicio, la propuesta tiene varios fallos.
example.gloss: In my judgement, the proposal has several flaws.

words.note: introduces a fact the speaker presents as undeniable, often after doubt has been raised

example.target: Lo cierto es que nadie sabe qué va a pasar.
example.gloss: The fact is that nobody knows what is going to happen.

words.note: introduces a surprising or unexpected fact, common in spoken narration

example.target: Resulta que el tren llegó una hora tarde.
example.gloss: It turns out that the train arrived an hour late.

words.note: opens the first side of an argument; pairs with por otra parte

example.target: Por una parte, el piso es barato.
example.gloss: On the one hand, the flat is cheap.

words.note: opens the second, contrasting side of an argument

example.target: Por otra parte, está muy lejos del centro.
example.gloss: On the other hand, it is very far from the centre.

words.note: formal, mainly written; introduces a conclusion drawn from what precedes

example.target: No hay billetes; así pues, tendremos que esperar al día siguiente.
example.gloss: There are no tickets; so, we will have to wait until the next day.

words.note: gives a reason, more formal than porque, can open the sentence

example.target: Puesto que ya es tarde, será mejor que nos vayamos.
example.gloss: Since it is already late, we had better leave.

words.note: gives a reason, neutral register, can open or follow the main clause

example.target: Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame con las maletas.
example.gloss: Since you are here, help me with the suitcases.

words.note: formal, gives a reason or premise, common in written Spanish

example.target: Dado que no hay más preguntas, damos por terminada la reunión.
example.gloss: Given that there are no more questions, we consider the meeting over.

words.note: introduces a consequence or a purpose; neutral register

example.target: Perdimos el autobús, de modo que llegamos tarde.
example.gloss: We missed the bus, so we arrived late.

words.note: formal written connector, rare in speech

example.target: El contrato incluye el alquiler; asimismo, cubre los gastos de comunidad.
example.gloss: The contract includes the rent; likewise, it covers the community fees.

words.note: shorter, common form of por lo tanto; states a logical conclusion

example.target: No hay entradas, por tanto, no podemos ir al concierto.
example.gloss: There are no tickets, therefore, we cannot go to the concert.

words.note: signals that the point holds regardless of what precedes; neutral

example.target: No sé si lloverá, pero en cualquier caso llevaré paraguas.
example.gloss: I do not know if it will rain, but in any case I will bring an umbrella.

words.note: spoken, introduces a qualification right after a positive statement

example.target: El piso es pequeño, eso sí, está muy bien situado.
example.gloss: The flat is small, mind you, it is very well located.

words.note: introduces a qualification or contrast; more formal than eso sí

example.target: El plan es bueno; ahora bien, necesitamos más tiempo.
example.gloss: The plan is good; now, we need more time.

words.note: signals that the speaker is moving on after making a point; neutral to formal

example.target: Dicho esto, creo que deberíamos votar.
example.gloss: That said, I think we should vote.

words.note: spoken equivalent of al parecer, reports something secondhand

example.target: Por lo visto, han cerrado la tienda de la esquina.
example.gloss: Apparently, they have closed the corner shop.

words.note: qualifies a statement as limited to the speaker's knowledge; contains the present subjunctive sepa

example.target: Que yo sepa, la reunión es a las cinco.
example.gloss: As far as I know, the meeting is at five.

words.note: signals that the speaker is being frank, often correcting an earlier impression

example.target: A decir verdad, no me apetece nada salir esta noche.
example.gloss: To tell you the truth, I do not feel like going out at all tonight.

words.note: softens or hedges a word choice

example.target: Es, por decirlo así, un poco cabezota.
example.gloss: He is, so to speak, a bit stubborn.

words.en: whatever the case, be that as it may
words.note: fixed expression built on the present subjunctive sea; neutral register

example.target: Sea como sea, tenemos que terminar el informe hoy.
example.gloss: Whatever happens, we have to finish the report today.

words.note: fixed expression built on the present subjunctive pase

example.target: Pase lo que pase, te voy a apoyar.
example.gloss: Whatever happens, I am going to support you.

words.note: hedges an approximate description; built on the present subjunctive digamos

example.target: Digamos que la reunión no salió como esperábamos.
example.gloss: Let us say that the meeting did not go as we expected.

words.en: at the end of the day, when all is said and done
words.note: sums up before a final judgement

example.target: A fin de cuentas, todos cometemos errores.
example.gloss: At the end of the day, we all make mistakes.

words.note: spoken discourse particle used to rephrase or sum up; colloquial, do not use in formal writing; not the same word as the verb form vamos (we go)

example.target: No me gusta el plan, vamos, que prefiero quedarme en casa.
example.gloss: I do not like the plan, I mean, I would rather stay home.

words.note: spoken, distinctly peninsular; used to encourage, agree, or close a conversation; very colloquial, do not use in writing

example.target: Venga, vámonos ya, que llegamos tarde.
example.gloss: Come on, let us go now, we are running late.

words.en: well, come on (as a discourse particle)
words.note: spoken discourse particle expressing mild surprise, protest, or emphasis; not the noun el hombre (man); colloquial, distinctly peninsular

example.target: Hombre, no me lo esperaba.
example.gloss: Well, I was not expecting that.

words.note: spoken, used to get the listener's attention before saying something, from the verb oír; colloquial

example.target: Oye, ¿sabes si va a llover mañana?
example.gloss: Hey, do you know if it is going to rain tomorrow?

words.en: would you believe it, look at that
words.note: spoken, introduces a surprising remark or invites the listener to notice something; colloquial, from fijarse

example.target: Fíjate, al final sí que aprobó el examen.
example.gloss: Would you believe it, he actually passed the exam in the end.

words.note: spoken, signals that an explanation is about to follow; colloquial

example.target: Verás, la cosa es un poco más complicada.
example.gloss: You see, the thing is a bit more complicated.

words.note: spoken, introduces a question, a check, or a moment of thought; very colloquial

example.target: A ver, ¿cuántos vais a venir a la cena?
example.gloss: Let's see, how many of you are coming to dinner?

words.note: spoken, closes a conversation or topic with resignation or simplicity; colloquial

example.target: Pues nada, ya hablamos otro día.
example.gloss: Well then, we will talk another day.

words.en: well, you know how it is
words.note: spoken, agrees with something unfortunate or ironic the listener already knows; colloquial

example.target: Ya ves, así es la vida.
example.gloss: Well, that is life for you.

words.note: spoken, strongly denies what was just said; colloquial, distinctly peninsular; an American speaker would more likely say para nada or de ninguna manera

example.target: ¿Estás enfadado? Qué va, para nada.
example.gloss: Are you angry? No way, not at all.

words.en: no way, out of the question
words.note: spoken, flatly refuses a suggestion; colloquial

example.target: ¿Salir con esta lluvia? Ni hablar.
example.gloss: Go out in this rain? No way.

words.en: of course, don't even mention it
words.note: spoken, distinctly peninsular; accepts a request generously or waves away thanks; a fixed courtesy expression, contains the conditional faltaría but is not a productive conditional construction

example.target: ¿Me puedes ayudar? Faltaría más.
example.gloss: Can you help me? Of course, no need to even ask.

words.note: spoken, enthusiastic confirmation; neutral to colloquial

example.target: ¿Vienes a la fiesta? Claro que sí.
example.gloss: Are you coming to the party? Of course I am.

words.note: strongly denies something, more formal than qué va or para nada, works in speech and writing

example.target: ¿Te molesta? En absoluto.
example.gloss: Does it bother you? Not at all.

words.note: spoken, denies something emphatically; colloquial, less formal than en absoluto

example.target: No me arrepiento para nada de la decisión.
example.gloss: I do not regret the decision at all.

words.note: signals a precaution taken against an unlikely event; neutral, spoken and written

example.target: Llévate el paraguas, por si acaso.
example.gloss: Take the umbrella, just in case.

words.note: signals that a point still holds despite what was just said; neutral

example.target: No creo que venga, pero avísale de todas formas.
example.gloss: I do not think he will come, but let him know anyway.

words.note: spoken, closes a topic with a note of resignation; colloquial to neutral

example.target: En fin, no se puede hacer nada más.
example.gloss: Well, there is nothing more that can be done.

words.note: spoken, summarises a long story before its outcome; colloquial

example.target: Perdimos el tren, discutimos con el taxista, total que llegamos dos horas tarde.
example.gloss: We missed the train, argued with the taxi driver, so anyway we arrived two hours late.

words.note: adds an extra, usually negative, fact; spoken and written

example.target: Llegó tarde y, encima, se había olvidado los documentos.
example.gloss: He arrived late and, on top of that, he had forgotten the documents.

words.note: spoken, distinctly peninsular; accepts a plan or checks the listener follows; very colloquial

example.target: ¿Nos vemos a las ocho? Vale.
example.gloss: Shall we meet at eight? Okay.

words.note: accepts a proposal or confirms agreement; neutral, less colloquial than vale

example.target: De acuerdo, quedamos mañana a las nueve.
example.gloss: Agreed, we will meet tomorrow at nine.

words.note: spoken, colloquial short form of no tengo ni idea

example.target: ¿Dónde está el mando? Ni idea.
example.gloss: Where is the remote? No idea.

words.note: spoken, colloquial, expresses vague uncertainty, often listing possibilities

example.target: Podríamos ir al cine, al teatro, qué sé yo.
example.gloss: We could go to the cinema, the theatre, whatever.

words.note: spoken, confirms that the listener has understood correctly; neutral to colloquial

example.target: Entonces, ¿el tren sale a las diez? Eso es.
example.gloss: So the train leaves at ten? That's right.

words.note: adds a remark in passing; slightly formal, spoken and written

example.target: El hotel, dicho sea de paso, era carísimo.
example.gloss: The hotel, by the way, was extremely expensive.

words.note: light-verb phrase; neutral register

example.target: Los domingos nos gusta dar un paseo por el parque.
example.gloss: On Sundays we like to take a walk in the park.

words.note: light-verb phrase, formal enough for a speech, also used casually

example.target: Quiero dar las gracias a todos los que ayudaron.
example.gloss: I want to thank everyone who helped.

words.en: to make one feel sorry, to be a pity
words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me da pena, nos da pena

example.target: Me da pena tirar la comida que sobra.
example.gloss: It makes me sad to throw away leftover food.

words.note: light-verb phrase, usually followed by a + person

example.target: Nunca hace caso a lo que le dicen.
example.gloss: He never pays attention to what he is told.

words.note: light-verb phrase, physical or emotional harm

example.target: Ten cuidado, ese cuchillo puede hacer daño.
example.gloss: Be careful, that knife can hurt you.

words.note: light-verb phrase; peninsular synonym llevar razón is in this same pack

example.target: Al final resultó que tenías razón.
example.gloss: In the end it turned out you were right.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Lo que dices no tiene mucho sentido.
example.gloss: What you are saying does not make much sense.

words.en: to bear in mind, to take into account
words.note: everyday light-verb phrase, less formal than the fixed formula hay que tener en cuenta

example.target: Ten en cuenta que el museo cierra a las seis.
example.gloss: Bear in mind that the museum closes at six.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: No puedo hablar ahora, tengo prisa.
example.gloss: I cannot talk now, I am in a hurry.

words.note: light-verb phrase, very common in the imperative

example.target: Ten cuidado al cruzar la calle.
example.gloss: Be careful when crossing the street.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Tuvimos mucha suerte con el tiempo durante el viaje.
example.gloss: We were very lucky with the weather during the trip.

words.en: to set in motion, to launch
words.note: light-verb phrase, common for starting a project or a machine

example.target: El ayuntamiento va a poner en marcha un nuevo programa de reciclaje.
example.gloss: The town council is going to launch a new recycling programme.

words.en: to lend a hand, to help out
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: ¿Me echas una mano con estas cajas?
example.gloss: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Voy a echar un vistazo al periódico antes de salir.
example.gloss: I am going to take a quick look at the newspaper before leaving.

words.note: light-verb phrase, more formal than decidir alone

example.target: Todavía no hemos tomado una decisión sobre el piso.
example.gloss: We still have not made a decision about the flat.

words.en: to take measures, to take action
words.note: light-verb phrase, often institutional

example.target: El gobierno anunció que va a tomar medidas contra la contaminación.
example.gloss: The government announced it is going to take measures against pollution.

words.note: formal light-verb phrase, common in written Spanish

example.target: La empresa va a llevar a cabo una reforma completa de la oficina.
example.gloss: The company is going to carry out a complete renovation of the office.

words.note: light-verb phrase, neutral to formal

example.target: Después de horas de negociación, llegaron a un acuerdo.
example.gloss: After hours of negotiation, they reached an agreement.

words.en: to make the most of, to benefit from
words.note: light-verb phrase, usually followed by de

example.target: Hay que sacar provecho de estas vacaciones.
example.gloss: We should make the most of this holiday.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Es pronto para sacar conclusiones sobre el resultado.
example.gloss: It is too early to draw conclusions about the result.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Al principio no quería ir, pero cambió de opinión.
example.gloss: At first he did not want to go, but he changed his mind.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: No te des por vencido tan pronto.
example.gloss: Do not give up so soon.

words.en: to be up to date, to be informed
words.note: light-verb phrase, usually followed by de

example.target: Intento estar al tanto de las noticias todos los días.
example.gloss: I try to stay informed about the news every day.

words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase, followed by a noun or infinitive

example.target: Estoy harto de esperar el autobús todos los días.
example.gloss: I am fed up with waiting for the bus every day.

words.en: to go blank, to draw a blank
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase, especially in an exam or a speech

example.target: Me puse muy nervioso y me quedé en blanco durante el examen.
example.gloss: I got very nervous and my mind went blank during the exam.

words.en: to put one's foot in it, to mess up
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: Metí la pata al mencionar su cumpleaños delante de todos.
example.gloss: I put my foot in it by mentioning her birthday in front of everyone.

words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: Al final, mi hermano siempre se sale con la suya.
example.gloss: In the end, my brother always gets his own way.

words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: Deja de dar rodeos y ve al grano.
example.gloss: Stop beating around the bush and get to the point.

words.en: to take for granted, to assume
words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: No des por hecho que va a venir.
example.gloss: Do not take it for granted that he is coming.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Al final tuvo que dar la razón a su hermana.
example.gloss: In the end he had to admit his sister was right.

words.en: to make someone angry, to be annoying
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me da rabia

example.target: Me da rabia perder el tiempo en el atasco.
example.gloss: It makes me angry to waste time in the traffic jam.

words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me da vergüenza

example.target: Le da vergüenza hablar en público.
example.gloss: He feels embarrassed speaking in public.

words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me da miedo

example.target: Esa película me da mucho miedo.
example.gloss: That film scares me a lot.

words.en: to do the favour of, please would you
words.note: formal, followed by an infinitive; often used in a scolding tone

example.target: Haz el favor de recoger tu habitación.
example.gloss: Do me the favour of tidying your room.

words.en: to make up, to make peace
words.note: light-verb phrase, after an argument

example.target: Después de la discusión, hicieron las paces enseguida.
example.gloss: After the argument, they made up right away.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Vamos a tener que hacer un esfuerzo para terminar a tiempo.
example.gloss: We are going to have to make an effort to finish on time.

words.en: to hit it off with someone
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase, usually with con

example.target: Los nuevos vecinos y nosotros hicimos buenas migas enseguida.
example.gloss: The new neighbours and we hit it off right away.

words.note: light-verb phrase, followed by a noun or a que clause

example.target: Todavía no tengo claro qué voy a estudiar.
example.gloss: I am still not clear about what I am going to study.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Tengo en mente un par de ideas para el regalo.
example.gloss: I have a couple of ideas in mind for the gift.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Hay que tener paciencia con los niños pequeños.
example.gloss: You have to be patient with small children.

words.note: formal light-verb phrase, mainly written

example.target: El informe pone de manifiesto varios problemas en la gestión.
example.gloss: The report reveals several problems in the management.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Nadie pone en duda su honestidad.
example.gloss: Nobody questions his honesty.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Es hora de poner en práctica lo que hemos aprendido.
example.gloss: It is time to put into practice what we have learned.

words.note: light-verb phrase, often followed by con

example.target: Te vas a poner en contacto con el técnico mañana.
example.gloss: You are going to get in touch with the technician tomorrow.

words.id: ponerse en la piel de otro
words.hr: ponerse en la piel de otro
words.en: to put oneself in someone else's shoes
words.note: figurative light-verb phrase

example.target: Antes de juzgar, hay que ponerse en la piel de otro.
example.gloss: Before judging, you have to put yourself in someone else's shoes.

words.note: light-verb phrase, often followed by a + person

example.target: Siempre me echa la culpa de todo.
example.gloss: He always blames me for everything.

words.en: to miss, to notice the lack of
words.note: light-verb phrase, more neutral than echar de menos

example.target: Echo en falta un poco más de organización.
example.gloss: I find there is a lack of a bit more organisation.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Nadie tomó en serio su advertencia.
example.gloss: Nobody took his warning seriously.

words.en: to tease, to pull someone's leg
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: ¿Me estás tomando el pelo?
example.gloss: Are you pulling my leg?

words.note: light-verb phrase, literal or figurative

example.target: Toma nota de la dirección antes de que se me olvide.
example.gloss: Take note of the address before I forget it.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Prefiero no tomar partido en esta discusión.
example.gloss: I prefer not to take sides in this argument.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Este trámite lleva tiempo, así que ten paciencia.
example.gloss: This procedure takes time, so be patient.

words.note: light-verb phrase, often habitual behaviour

example.target: Le encanta llevar la contraria en todas las conversaciones.
example.gloss: He loves contradicting people in every conversation.

words.note: light-verb phrase, close in meaning to sacar provecho

example.target: Hay que saber sacar partido a las oportunidades.
example.gloss: You have to know how to make the most of opportunities.

words.en: to drive someone mad, to exasperate
words.note: colloquial light-verb phrase

example.target: Ese ruido me saca de quicio.
example.gloss: That noise drives me crazy.

words.en: to bring to success, to raise (a family, a project)
words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Consiguieron sacar adelante el proyecto pese a los problemas.
example.gloss: They managed to make the project succeed despite the problems.

words.en: to get by, to pull through
words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Con esfuerzo, la familia consiguió salir adelante.
example.gloss: With effort, the family managed to get by.

words.en: to come out ahead, to benefit
words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Al final, todos salimos ganando con el nuevo horario.
example.gloss: In the end, we all came out ahead with the new schedule.

words.en: to come out worse off, to lose out
words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Si cancelamos el contrato ahora, salimos perdiendo.
example.gloss: If we cancel the contract now, we come out worse off.

words.en: to make a bad impression, to dislike someone
words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me cae mal

example.target: No sé por qué, pero ese actor me cae mal.
example.gloss: I do not know why, but I do not like that actor.

words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me viene bien

example.target: ¿Te viene bien quedar el sábado?
example.gloss: Does it suit you to meet on Saturday?

words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me viene mal

example.target: Me viene mal el jueves, ¿podemos quedar otro día?
example.gloss: Thursday is inconvenient for me, can we meet another day?

words.en: to be hard for someone to do
words.note: light-verb phrase, works like gustar: me cuesta trabajo

example.target: Me cuesta trabajo levantarme tan temprano.
example.gloss: It is hard for me to get up so early.

words.note: figurative light-verb phrase

example.target: Tantas horas sin dormir acaban pasando factura.
example.gloss: So many hours without sleep end up taking their toll.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: Vamos a pasarlo bien esta noche, ya veréis.
example.gloss: We are going to have a great time tonight, you'll see.

words.note: light-verb phrase

example.target: No quiero pasarlo mal en el viaje, así que lo he organizado todo.
example.gloss: I do not want to have a bad time on the trip, so I have planned everything.

words.note: fixed expression

example.target: Si el plan va a funcionar está por ver.
example.gloss: Whether the plan will work remains to be seen.

words.note: fixed expression

example.target: En esta reunión está en juego el futuro de la empresa.
example.gloss: The future of the company is at stake in this meeting.

words.en: to be made clear, to become clear
words.note: light-verb phrase, often impersonal; que quede claro takes the present subjunctive

example.target: Que quede claro que no fue culpa mía.
example.gloss: Let it be clear that it was not my fault.

words.note: light-verb phrase, active counterpart of quedar claro

example.target: El director dejó claro que no habrá más cambios.
example.gloss: The director made it clear that there will be no more changes.
